record_type_quote: In summary, we report a direct replication of Muffato et al. (2019) and provide evidence for age-related differences in spatial encoding strategies, which are related to place recognition performance.

targets.authors: Muffato V., Hilton C., Meneghetti C., De Beni R., Wiener J. M.
targets.title: Evidence for age-related deficits in object-location binding during place recognition
targets.evidence_quote: In the present experiment, we used eye-tracking to study if the age-related difference in place recognition ability reported by Muffato et al. (2019) was the result of different place encoding strategies. We expected to replicate behavioural results from their study.
targets.outcome_quote: The behavioural results of this study are a direct replication of those found by Muffato et al. (2019) . As such, the main results are that older adults are impaired in object-location binding dependent place recognition but have preserved perspective taking ability.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall verdict about behavioural results takes precedence over the one contrast on incremental 30–60 degree perspective shifts. Eye movement findings against other studies are explanatory comparisons, not additional replication targets.

reasoning: New participants directly re-test Muffato et al. with added eye tracking. Title and full author list verified in the full article.
